conclusion: The prior carrier-exactification result is deliberately scoped: it is a carrier-exactification statement on the fixed Route A flagship support, not a public event package and not a public carrier theorem. Its lawful object is a refined same-branch witness; its public-side object is a coarse signature shadow. The relationship between the two is non-faithful: public signatures retain operational readout information but do not determine the refined law-bearing carrier data. In standard ontic/epistemic language , the public shadow is an epistemic image of the carrier; in Markov-chain language , the carrier-to-public map is lumpable only in a restricted sense. Throughout this paper we refer to these objects descriptively — the refined witness (lawful, carrier-side), the public signature shadow (coarse, readout-side), and the witness-to-shadow basis that relates them without supplying a faithful inverse. The corresponding machine-readable identifiers are listed once, in Appendix . Consequently the public shadow can supply public/readout-side predicates for later bridge records, but it cannot by itself supply lawful carrier structure or shared-event identity.
